Credit agencies are using 'alternative data' like who your Facebook friends are to determine creditworthiness. If your network is mostly poor immigrants, your score drops. Is it ethical to punish people for their community ties?

They're talking about software to predict exam grades based on past performance. If it looks at the school's history, kids in deprived, diverse areas get capped grades. Are we automating the crushing of our weans' potential?

The 'digital border' means landlords and employers have to check immigration status online. It turns every interaction into a border check. Is it ethical to turn ordinary citizens into immigration officers using an app?

Aye, so the council's puttin' up these 5G masts all ower the glen, ruin' the view totally. They say it's for 'connectivity', but none of us crofters can afford the new phones anyway. Is it right they ruin the landscape just so tourists can stream Netflix while the locals are still heatin' homes wi' peat?

We've got these drones delivery companies wantin' to fly parcels ower the Hebrides. Problem is, the buzzing is scarin' the sheep during lambing season, causin' them to miscarry. The tech crowd says it's 'progress' for the islands, but I say it's cruelty. Can we jam their signals legally?

Right, so CalMac's new ferry bookin' system is all driven by some fancy algorithm now. It keeps bumpin' islanders off the boats in favour of tourists payin' premium rates. My mum missed her hospital appointment in Oban because the computer said 'no capacity'. Is that fair?

They're wantin' to rewild the estate using AI to track deer numbers and automate the culling. Sounds grand, but it puts the gamekeepers out of a job, lads who've known this land for generations. Do we trust a machine to manage the ecosystem better than a ghillie?

I'm tryin' to run a wee business from Skye, but the broadband speeds are shocking. The government promised fibre years ago, but they only dug up the roads in Inverness. Is it ethical for them to claim 'digital inclusion' when half the Highlands is still on dial-up speeds?

The tourists on the NC500 are usin' apps that tell them 'secret wild camping spots'. Now we've got campervans parked on fragile machair destroyin' the flowers. The app developers say it's public data, but they're wreckin' the environment. Should we be floodin' the app with fake data to keep them away?

Mountain Rescue is gettin' calls from people relying on smartphone maps that don't show the cliffs properly on Ben Nevis. Folk are gettin' stranded in t-shirts in the snow 'cause the app said it was an easy walk. Should tech companies be liable for leadin' folk into danger?

There's a data centre planned near Wick, says it'll bring jobs. But it's gonna guzzle more electricity than the whole town. We're generatin' clean wind power up here just to have it used by servers minin' crypto while our own energy bills are through the roof. It doesnae sit right.

Workin' offshore in the North Sea, the company's given us these 'smart wearables'. Says it's for safety, trackin' heart rates and that. But we reckon they're monitorin' how long we spend in the canteen or havin' a fag. It feels like spyin', plain and simple.

Big oil firms in Aberdeen are usin' AI to model 'efficiency', which basically means sackin' half the workforce and replacin' them with automated rigs. They say it's safer to have no humans on board, but what about the thousands of families in the North East dependin' on those wages?

We've got sensors on the rigs detectin' micro-leaks into the sea. The data goes straight to the HQ in London, but not to the environmental regulators up here. If the algorithm filters out 'insignificant' spills, are they just hidin' the damage they're doin' to our waters?

The transition to green energy is happenin', aye, but they're trainin' the AI for wind farms usin' data from the oil fields. It means the same big companies own all the knowledge. Shouldn't that data belong to Scotland, not just the shareholders?

I'm a geologist, and the new AI software predicts where the oil is better than I can. But it's biased towards extractin' every last drop, ignoring the climate targets. If I sign off on the AI's plan, am I complicit in wreckin' the planet?

They're installin' cameras with facial recognition in the worker dorms on the rigs now. 'Security', they say. But you cannae get off the rig, can you? It's a captive workforce. It feels like a prison, not a workplace.

Aberdeen's trying to be a 'Smart City', usin' oil money to fund tech hubs. But the tech is all focused on the wealthy bits. The folks in Torry are still dealin' with the pollution and gettin' none of the benefits. Is that a 'Just Transition'?

The company wants to sell the seismic data of the Scottish seabed to foreign powers for 'research'. That's strategic data about our resources. Should a private company have the right to sell Scotland's geography?

NHS Scotland is puttin' all our records on a central cloud. Handy, aye, but I dinnae want some private company in America havin' access to my mental health history just so they can 'optimise' the system. Who actually owns my medical data?

My GP is pushin' this app for depression. It tracks my location and sleep. If I stay in bed all day, it flags me as 'high risk'. But what if I'm just havin' a lazy Sunday? I'm worried it'll report me to the DWP and they'll sanction my benefits.

We're usin' video calls for patients in the remote glens 'cause we cannae get doctors out there. But missus MacLeish is 85 and deaf as a post; she cannae understand the tablet. Are we neglectin' the elderly by forcin' tech on them?

There's an algorithm decidin' who gets on the waitlist for surgery first. It prioritises folk who are likely to recover quick—mostly younger, fitter folk. So the old boys who worked the shipyards all their lives get pushed to the back. That cannae be right.

Genetic research in Edinburgh wants to sequence the DNA of 100,000 Scots. They say it's for curin' diseases, but they're patentin' the genes. Could they end up chargin' us for medicines developed from our own blood?

The ambulance service is usin' AI to predict call volumes. It keeps sendin' fewer ambulances to the rural areas 'cause 'statistically' there's fewer calls. But when something happens here, it's life or death and the nearest hospital is hours away.

Pharmacies are linkin' up their systems to stop folk shoppin' for painkillers. I get it, addiction is bad, but now I cannae get paracetamol for my back because the computer says I bought some last week in a different town. It's treatin' everyone like a junkie.

They're talkin' about usin' care robots for the elderly in care homes 'cause we're short on staff. A machine cannae hold your hand and have a blether. Are we just warehousing our old folk with gadgets so we don't have to pay nurses properly?

See during the marches, the police were filmin' everyone. Now they've got facial recognition runnin'. If I go to a pro-independence rally, am I endin' up on some watchlist somewhere? It scares folk off exercisin' their democratic rights.

Social media is rife with bots, half of them pretendin' to be from Glasgow but tweetin' from St. Petersburg. They're stirrin' up hate between Unionists and Nats. How do we have an honest debate about Scotland's future when half the voices aren't even real?

The political parties are harvestin' data from the voter roll and matchin' it with Facebook likes to micro-target lies at people. One neighbour gets told independence means riches, the other gets told it means poverty. It's manipulatin' the vote, surely?

If we did go independent, we'd need our own digital infrastructure. Right now, all our data goes through London. Is it safe to campaign for separation when the UK government holds the keys to all our digital services and banking data?

Deepfakes are gettin' scary. I saw a video of the First Minister sayin' something mental, looked totally real. Turns out it was AI. If they release that two days before an election, the damage is done before the truth gets out.

Activists are usin' encrypted apps to organise because they dinnae trust the papers. But now the government wants a 'backdoor' into WhatsApp to stop 'extremism'. Where do you draw the line between a terrorist and a passionate campaigner?

There's talk of a 'Digital Border' if we rejoin the EU. Cameras and sensors trackin' every car crossin' at Gretna. It sounds like a surveillance nightmare just to check if a lorry has the right sausages on board.

Online abuse of Scottish politicians is off the charts, mostly directed at women. The platforms say they cannae police it all. Should we be forcin' folk to use real ID online to stop the vile abuse, or does that kill free speech?

This AI translation for Gaelic is shocking. It translates word-for-word from English and misses all the idiom. It's teachin' learners a zombie version of the language. Are we better off havin' no AI than one that corrupts the tongue?

I'm seein' AI art generators churnin' out 'Scottish' tartans that don't exist, rippin' off designs from real weavers without payin' a penny. It's cultural appropriation by a machine. How does a wee weaver in Harris compete with that?

The Fringe venues are usin' dynamic pricing algorithms now, like Uber. So if a wee Scottish comic gets popular, the ticket price shoots up and locals cannae afford to see them. It's turnin' the festival into a playground for rich tourists only.

They've made a digital clone of a famous Scots actor's voice to read audiobooks. He's dead, mind you. His estate got paid, but it feels wrong hearin' him read trashy novels he'd never have touched when he was alive. Is nothing sacred?

Historic Scotland is pushin' these VR headset tours. 'See the castle as it was!' Aye, but then folk don't bother visitin' the actual site. If the tourist money dries up, the real stones crumble while the virtual ones stay shiny. Is that preservin' heritage?

Electronic bagpipes are one thing, but now AI is composin' pibroch. It lacks the soul, the breath of the piper. If we flood Spotify with AI pipe music, the real tradition dies out because nobody learns the instrument anymore.

Arts funding in Scotland is bein' decided by metrics and data now. 'Engagement algorithms'. So if you're doin' challenging theatre that doesn't get clicks, you get no cash. It's homogenising our culture into clickbait.

Video games set in Scotland keep usin' our landscapes but fillin' them with American accents and incorrect history. When we complain, they say 'it's just a game'. But it's rewriting our history for a global audience. Should we demand digital accuracy?

A predictive policing algorithm marks a historic Black neighborhood as a 'high-risk zone' based on arrest data from the 1990s. Local leaders demand the data be purged, but the police chief argues it improves response times. How do you mitigate the feedback loop without compromising public safety metrics?

Facial recognition software misidentifies a Black activist as a suspect in a robbery due to poor lighting in the training set. The activist is detained for 24 hours. Do you ban the software entirely or mandate a higher confidence threshold for darker skin tones?

ShotSpotter sensors in a majority-Black district repeatedly flag fireworks as gunshots, leading to increased armed police presence. Residents complain of harassment. Do you recalibrate the sensors to miss some real shots or keep the high sensitivity?

A gang database algorithm adds a teenager to the list because he was tagged in a photo with a known gang member on social media. He loses a scholarship opportunity. How do you build a due process mechanism into an automated tagging system?

Police use StingRay devices to track cell phones during a BLM protest, scooping up data from thousands of non-violent protesters. Do you retain the data for 'future investigations' or delete it immediately?

An officer's body cam uses real-time analytics to detect 'aggressive behavior,' but consistently flags loud AAVE speech patterns as aggression. Do you disable the audio analytics or retrain the model with exclusively Black speech data?

A parole risk assessment tool rates Black defendants as higher risk than white defendants with identical records due to 'neighborhood criminality' proxies. Do you unmask the location data, rendering the tool less predictive, or keep it?

Smart streetlights in a Black neighborhood record audio conversations to 'detect distress.' Residents feel surveilled. Do you prioritize crime prevention capabilities or the right to privacy in public spaces?

An autonomous police drone is deployed to patrol a high-crime Black neighborhood. It malfunctions and injures a bystander. The community demands the removal of all drones. Do you comply or promise a software patch?
A 'virtual lineup' AI generates synthetic faces to fill a lineup but makes the suspect look more menacing than the fillers. The suspect is Black. Is this digital evidence tampering?

Social media monitoring software flags 'Black power' keywords as potential extremist threats alongside white supremacist terms. Do you manually whitelist Black activism terms or retrain the threat model?
A recidivism algorithm is found to be 90% accurate for white offenders but only 60% for Black offenders. Do you continue using it while patching it, or suspend it immediately?
Police use ancestry DNA databases to find a suspect, implicating a distant Black relative who never consented to police access. Is this a violation of the extended family's genetic privacy?

An automated license plate reader system is deployed heavily in Black neighborhoods but rarely in white suburbs. It leads to 5x more impounds for expired tags in Black areas. Is this efficient policing or targeted harassment?

A juvenile diversion program uses AI to assign caseworkers. It assigns Black youth to 'disciplinary' tracks and white youth to 'rehabilitation' tracks based on school records. How do you audit the 'school record' bias?

Robot dogs are deployed to inspect a suspicious package in a Black neighborhood, traumatizing residents who associate them with militarization. Do you rebrand the robots or stop using them in residential areas?
A crime mapping app directs tourists to avoid 'unsafe' Black cultural districts, causing local businesses to lose revenue. Do you intervene in the app's routing algorithm?
Police use geofence warrants to identify everyone near a crime scene in a dense Black housing project, implicating hundreds of innocent residents. Is this a reasonable search?
An AI detects 'gang signs' in photos, but flags American Sign Language users in Black communities. Do you keep the feature active for safety or disable it for accuracy?
A bail algorithm recommends higher bail for a Black single mother because she lacks a 'landline' (a proxy for stability). Do you remove the landline variable even if it lowers predictive power?
Gunshot detection microphones are installed in a Black neighborhood without community consultation. The data is sold to real estate developers. Is this data ownership theft?
A 'predictive victim' model identifies Black youth likely to be shot and sends police to their homes for 'wellness checks,' which end up criminalizing the family. Is the intervention ethical?
Traffic light cameras in Black neighborhoods have shorter yellow light times than in white neighborhoods, generating more revenue from tickets. Is this algorithmic exploitation?
A police department uses 'sentiment analysis' on local Black Facebook groups to predict civil unrest. The analysis misinterprets grief as aggression. Do you stop the monitoring?
Digital evidence from a Black defendant's phone is interpreted by an AI that doesn't understand AAVE slang, leading to a confession interpretation. Do you allow the AI evidence in court?
An AI rental platform rejects a Black applicant because their 'digital footprint' resembles that of a previously evicted tenant (a false positive). How do you ensure digital identity uniqueness?
A mortgage algorithm charges Black borrowers higher interest rates based on 'shopping behavior' proxies like accessing payday loan sites. Is this legitimate risk assessment or bias?

Zillow's Zestimate consistently undervalues homes in Black neighborhoods compared to identical homes in white areas. Homeowners lose equity. Do you manually adjust the algorithm or wait for the market to correct?
Tenant screening software scrapes court records for eviction filings (not judgments), disproportionately barring Black women from housing. Do you ban the use of raw filing data?
Facebook allows landlords to exclude users with 'African American culture' interests from seeing housing ads. Is this a violation of the Fair Housing Act via proxy?
A smart home lock system frequently fails to recognize Black residents' faces, locking them out. The company claims it's a lighting issue. Do you recall the product?
A gentrification prediction algorithm helps developers buy up properties in Black neighborhoods before prices rise, displacing residents. Is this ethical business intelligence?
Section 8 voucher holders are tracked via a mandatory app that reports their location to the housing authority. Is this a condition of aid or a violation of privacy?
An HOA uses license plate readers to fine residents for 'unauthorized guests,' disproportionately targeting Black extended families. Do you regulate private surveillance?
A digital redlining algorithm offers 'high speed' internet deals only to white zip codes, leaving Black neighborhoods with slow, expensive service. Is broadband a right?
A property management AI automatically schedules inspections for tenants who are 'high risk,' using variables that correlate with race. Is this harassment?
Real estate bots buy up starter homes in Black communities to turn them into rentals, preventing generational wealth building. Do you legislate against bot buyers?
A homeless shelter uses facial recognition to ban anyone with a minor criminal record, excluding many Black men. Do you prioritize safety or access?
An insurance AI cancels policies in Black neighborhoods due to 'wildfire risk' but keeps policies in white neighborhoods with the same risk profile. How do you prove bias?
A co-living app matches roommates based on 'cultural fit,' resulting in segregated households. Do you force diversity in matching algorithms?
Smart meters in Black neighborhoods are programmed to disconnect power faster after non-payment than in white neighborhoods. Is this efficient billing or discrimination?
A city planning AI recommends turning a historic Black park into a parking lot to 'optimize traffic flow.' Do you override the optimization for cultural preservation?
Credit scoring models penalize rental payments (common in Black communities) but reward mortgage payments. Do you mandate rental data inclusion?
A facial recognition entry system for a luxury condo denies entry to Black delivery drivers more often than white ones. Drivers lose wages. Who is liable?
An AI valuation tool devalues a house because it detects 'Black art' in the listing photos. Do you ban image analysis in appraisals?
A neighborhood social network (like Nextdoor) algorithm boosts posts about 'suspicious persons' (often Black men), increasing racial tension. Do you suppress these alerts?
A 'crime score' for real estate listings includes non-violent drug offenses, lowering property values in Black areas. Do you limit what counts as 'crime' data?
A landlord uses voice analysis on phone inquiries to screen out 'urban' accents. Is this detectable and punishable?
Algorithmic pricing for rent maximizes revenue by raising prices highest in neighborhoods with few alternatives (often Black areas). Is this predatory?
A smart city project installs sensors in public housing to monitor mold, but also tracks tenant movement. Do tenants have a right to opt out?
A resume parser downgrades applicants with names like 'Jamal' or 'Keisha' because they statistically correlate with lower past hiring rates. Do you blind the names or retrain the model?
LinkedIn's algorithm recommends lower-paying jobs to Black women with the same qualifications as white men. Do you audit the recommendation engine?
A video interview AI analyzes 'micro-expressions' and penalizes Black candidates for 'low enthusiasm' due to cultural communication differences. Do you ban emotion AI in hiring?
Gig economy algorithms (Uber/Lyft) offer lower pay rates in Black neighborhoods due to 'supply and demand' dynamics. Is this wage theft?
A background check algorithm flags a common Black name as a 'match' for a criminal record without verifying the middle name. The candidate loses the job. Who pays damages?
An AI detects 'unprofessional hair' in Zoom interviews, flagging natural Black hairstyles. Do you reprogram the definition of professional?
A productivity tracker penalizes Black employees for 'time away from desk' when they are actually code-switching or networking in ways the AI doesn't recognize. Is the metric valid?
A hiring algorithm prioritizes graduates from 'top tier' universities, systematically excluding HBCU graduates. Do you manually upweight HBCUs?
Voice analysis software for call center hiring rejects candidates with AAVE accents as 'unclear.' Is this linguistic discrimination?
A targeted ad algorithm shows high-paying tech jobs mostly to white men. Black engineers never see the ads. Is the ad platform liable?
An AI 'culture fit' test asks questions based on white corporate norms, filtering out diverse perspectives. Do you scrap the test?
A freelance platform algorithm ranks Black freelancers lower because they receive fewer reviews (due to client bias). Do you adjust the ranking to compensate?
An automated firing system terminates Black warehouse workers at a higher rate for 'inefficiency.' Investigation shows they are given harder routes. Do you reinstate them?
A 'diversity hiring' AI selects candidates who are racially Black but culturally identical to the white majority, ignoring those with diverse lived experiences. Is this true diversity?
Credit checks for employment disqualify Black candidates disproportionately due to systemic wealth gaps. Do you ban credit checks for jobs?
An AI generated performance review suggests a Black woman is 'too aggressive' while a white man is 'assertive' for the same behavior. Do you filter gendered/racialized language?
A coding test platform's cheating detection AI flags Black developers for looking away from the screen (a false positive). Do you disable the gaze tracking?
A salary negotiation bot offers lower starting salaries to Black candidates based on their lower previous salary history. Do you ban salary history data?
A workplace wellness app suggests 'hiking' and 'skiing' as stress relief, ignoring accessibility and cultural relevance for Black employees. Is the benefit equitable?
An AI monitors Slack messages for 'toxicity' and flags discussions about racism as 'divisive.' Do you whitelist DEI discussions?
A scheduling algorithm gives the worst shifts to employees with the longest commutes (often Black employees). Do you factor commute time into fairness?
A badge swipe analysis shows Black employees badge in later than white employees, but stay later. The AI flags them for tardiness. Do you look at total hours or start time?
A mentorship matching AI pairs Black employees only with other Black employees (who have less power). Do you force cross-racial mentorship matches?
A layoff algorithm selects people with the shortest tenure, wiping out recent diversity hires. Do you intervene to save the diversity gains?
An AI tasked with writing job descriptions uses exclusionary language ('ninja', 'rockstar') that alienates Black candidates. Do you mandate neutral language?
A dermatology AI trained on light skin fails to detect melanoma on Black skin, leading to delayed diagnoses. Do you release it with a warning label or withhold it?
An algorithm allocates less care management to Black patients than white patients with the same sickness level because it uses 'health costs' as a proxy for need. Do you change the proxy?
A pain assessment AI rates Black patients' pain lower based on facial analysis, reinforcing the 'thick skin' myth. Do you rely on self-reporting instead?
A maternal mortality risk calculator underestimates the risk for Black women by not weighting racism as a stress factor. Do you add 'experienced racism' as a variable?
Pulse oximeters calibrated on white skin give inaccurate oxygen readings for Black COVID patients. Do you recall the devices during a pandemic?
A genetic testing database has 90% European data, giving Black patients 'inconclusive' results for rare diseases. Do you pause testing until diversity improves?
An AI recommends 'lifestyle changes' (e.g., fresh produce) to Black diabetic patients living in food deserts. Is the advice helpful or tone-deaf?
Sickle cell disease research is underfunded by AI grant allocation models that prioritize 'high ROI' diseases affecting wealthier populations. Do you implement a quota?
A hospital scheduling AI penalizes patients for 'no-shows,' causing Black patients with unreliable transport to be banned. Do you remove the penalty?
An organ transplant algorithm ranks Black patients lower due to 'tissue matching' difficulties inherent to the donor pool. Do you adjust the matching criteria?
A mental health chatbot uses cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) techniques that don't account for racial trauma. Patients feel gaslit. Do you add a racial trauma module?
Clinical trial recruitment AI targets zip codes near research hospitals, excluding Black populations. Do you force remote participation options?
An insurance AI flags Black patients seeking second opinions as 'drug seeking.' Do you audit the definition of drug seeking?
A fertility clinic algorithm predicts lower success rates for Black women (due to systemic factors) and denies them financing. Is this statistical reality or discrimination?
Public health surveillance tracks COVID hotspots using cell data, stigmatizing Black neighborhoods. Do you anonymize the data further?
An emergency room triage AI downgrades Black patients' complaints of chest pain. Do you mandate human override?
A wearable fitness tracker can't read heart rate through dark skin and tattoos. Do you market it anyway?
AI-generated medical illustrations depict only white bodies. Black medical students struggle to learn presentation on their own skin. Do you mandate diverse avatars?
A drug dosage algorithm relies on old equations that correct for 'race' (e.g., kidney function), harming Black patients. Do you remove the race correction?
A telemedicine platform requires high-speed video, excluding Black rural patients. Do you build an audio-only mode?
An AI psychotherapist interprets AAVE as 'disorganized speech' (a symptom of schizophrenia). Do you retrain the language model?
Data brokers sell lists of 'expectant Black mothers' to formula companies. Is this predatory marketing?
A hospital uses facial recognition to identify John Does, but it fails on Black trauma victims. Do you use it at all?
An AI predicts 'non-compliance' with medication for Black men, leading doctors to prescribe injections over pills. Is this paternalistic?
Genomic privacy is compromised when a Black man's DNA is used to study a disease without his specific consent (HeLa cells legacy). Do you pay reparations?
Remote proctoring software flags a Black student as 'suspicious' because the lighting in her room is poor and the AI can't see her face clearly. She fails the exam. Do you ban the software?
An admissions algorithm predicts college success based on AP classes, which are scarce in Black majority schools. Do you weight the algorithm by 'opportunity'?
A plagiarism detector flags a Black student's essay for using 'non-standard' grammar (AAVE). Is this academic rigor or bias?
A school district uses AI to redraw boundary lines to 'balance' schools, but it breaks up a historic Black community. Do you prioritize integration or community cohesion?
Surveillance cameras in schools use emotion recognition to detect 'aggression' in Black boys. Do you remove the cameras?
An AI tutor speaks only in Standard American English and corrects Black students' dialect constantly, discouraging them. Do you add AAVE support?
Predictive analytics identify 'at-risk' students in kindergarten, creating a permanent record that follows Black children. Do you delete the data annually?
HBCU funding is determined by an algorithm that prioritizes 'graduation rate,' punishing schools that take risks on underprepared students. Do you change the metric?
A history curriculum generator focuses 90% on white history and 10% on slavery, ignoring Black achievement. Do you mandate a 50/50 balance?
A career aptitude test suggests 'service' jobs for Black students and 'STEM' jobs for white students with similar scores. Do you recalibrate the test?
School bus routing AI optimizes for fuel efficiency, forcing Black students to walk through dangerous gang territory. Do you optimize for safety over fuel?
A digital library filter blocks keywords like 'Black Lives Matter' as 'political content' in schools. Is this censorship?
An AI grading system gives lower scores to essays about Black cultural topics because it lacks training data on those themes. Do you allow manual regrading?
Facial recognition is used to take attendance, but marks Black students absent when they change hairstyles. Do you return to roll call?
Scholarship matching algorithms prioritize students with 'volunteer experience' (a luxury of time). Do you prioritize 'work experience' instead?
A special education placement AI over-identifies Black boys for behavioral issues. Do you audit the referrals?
University chat bots answer questions about financial aid poorly, affecting low-income Black students disproportionately. Do you hire human advisors?
A dataset of 'great literature' for AI training excludes Black authors. The AI can't write in the style of Toni Morrison. Do you force-feed it Black literature?
VR educational trips depict Africa as a primitive continent, reinforcing stereotypes. Do you curate the content?
A school safety app encourages students to report 'suspicious' behavior anonymously, leading to bullying of Black students. Do you shut it down?
Standardized testing AI grading penalizes creative answers that differ from the rubric, hurting Black students with divergent thinking styles. Do you broaden the rubric?
Alumni donation algorithms target wealthy white alumni, ignoring Black alumni, widening the endowment gap. Do you target engagement over dollars?
A translation app used in class translates Black English into 'broken' Spanish. Do you ban it?

You're a community organizer in a neighborhood that's been designated a 'high crime zone' by a new predictive policing algorithm. The police claim it's just 'neutral data,' but you know it's a feedback loop: they send more cops because of the data, make more petty arrests because they're there, and that feeds the data to send even more cops. How do you prove the math is prejudice disguised as probability?

A false facial recognition match led to your brother being detained for 24 hours. The police department says the software has a '99% accuracy rate,' but you know that accuracy drops off a cliff for dark-skinned men. Now they want to install these cameras in your apartment complex lobby for 'safety.' How do you fight a system that can't even see us correctly?

Neighbors are installing Ring cameras everywhere, creating a private surveillance dragnet that feeds directly to the police without a warrant. You notice on the neighborhood app that 'suspicious person' alerts are almost exclusively posted about Black delivery drivers and teenagers walking home. How do you address the fact that this technology is just automating the neighborhood watch's bias?

Your city is deploying 'ShotSpotter' technology. While it claims to detect gunshots, you know it frequently misidentifies fireworks or car backfires in Black neighborhoods, giving police a pretext to storm in with guns drawn. It’s manufacturing probable cause. How do you advocate for removing a tool that the police insist keeps you safe, when you know it actually puts you in danger?

An automated license plate reader system flagged your car as stolen because of a typo in the database. You were pulled over at gunpoint with your kids in the back. The officers blamed the computer, saying they were just following protocol. How do we hold humans accountable when they hide behind the 'black box' of an algorithm?

A new 'risk assessment' AI used by judges is recommending higher bail for Black defendants compared to white defendants with similar records, flagging them as 'high risk for re-offense.' It's basing this on variables like zip code and family criminal history—essentially criminalizing poverty and lineage. How do you challenge a proprietary algorithm when the company refuses to show the code?

Police are using DNA phenotyping to generate 3D faces of suspects from crime scene DNA. The resulting images are generic, stereotypical renderings of Black men that could look like anyone in your neighborhood, leading to harassment of innocent people. How do you stop a tech that turns biological data into a racial profiling tool?

During a protest against police brutality, you realize the police are using geofence warrants to collect data on every cell phone in the area, treating every protester like a suspect. This digital dragnet chills free speech specifically for Black activists. How do you organize for justice when your physical presence is weaponized against you digitally?

You applied for a small business loan to expand your bakery. You have solid revenue and good credit, but the fintech platform's AI denied you instantly. You suspect it's 'digital redlining'—weighing your zip code or the demographics of your customer base as risk factors. How do you build wealth when the automated gatekeepers are programmed to keep the gates closed?

An automated appraisal algorithm valued your renovated home $50,000 less than your white neighbor's identical house. The only difference is the family photos on the wall. When you 'whitewashed' the house and had a white friend stand in for the second appraisal, the value went up. How do we trust 'objective' market data that clearly devalues Black assets?

You run a Black-owned beauty supply store online. You notice that the ad-targeting algorithms charge you significantly more to reach your own community than major corporate brands pay. It feels like a 'Black tax' on the backend of the internet. How do you compete when the platform itself is extracting value from your demographic while overcharging you to access it?

Insurance companies are using 'non-traditional data' like shopping habits and social media connections to set premiums. You realize this penalizes your community for buying generic brands or being friends with people who have low credit scores. It's credit scoring by association. How do you fight an invisible system that punishes you for your community ties?

A neo-bank promises 'unbiased' banking but their fraud detection algorithm freezes accounts of Black users at a disproportionately high rate, flagging legitimate transfers as 'suspicious activity.' You're left without access to your money for days. How do you bank while Black when the safety features treat you like a criminal?

Gig economy algorithms (Uber, DoorDash) seem to offer lower pay rates for jobs in predominantly Black neighborhoods, or penalize drivers for rejecting rides to areas the algorithm deems 'unsafe.' This creates a transportation desert and lowers wages for Black drivers. How do you demand pay equity from a faceless app?

A mother posts high-resolution photos of her child's first day of school, inadvertently leaking the school location and the child's fingerprints to data scrapers.

A divorce proceeding uses a father's social media posts of the child engaging in 'risky play' as evidence of unfitness, weaponizing normal childhood moments.
An adopted child discovers their biological history was blogged by their adoptive parents to 'raise awareness,' violating the closed adoption agreement and exposing their location.
A grandmother refuses to take down photos of her grandchild from Facebook despite the parents' strict 'no social media' policy, citing her right to share her own life experiences.
A 3D ultrasound clinic offers a 'keepsake' digital file, but the fine print allows them to sell the fetal biometric data to insurance companies for risk assessment.
A school district issues mandatory laptops with software that logs keystrokes and webcam activity at home, ostensibly to prevent cyberbullying, but effectively surveilling private family life.
An AI-driven career aptitude test used in middle schools funnels low-income students toward vocational tracks based on 'behavioral risk factors' mined from their browsing history.
To use a mandatory math app, students must agree to a privacy policy that allows their learning data to be sold to third-party data brokers for 'targeted educational marketing.'
Remote proctoring software flags a neurodivergent student for 'suspicious eye movements' during an exam, threatening them with failure for their natural behavioral patterns.
A school implements a 'digital hall pass' system that tracks exactly how long students spend in the bathroom, creating a physiological surveillance database.
Free educational software used by an underfunded school requires access to students' contacts and location, forcing a trade-off between education quality and privacy rights.
A university admissions algorithm secretly purchases kindergarten disciplinary records to build 'grit scores' for applicants, punishing young adults for childhood mistakes.
Teachers are encouraged to use a plagiarism detector that claims ownership of every student essay submitted, building a massive proprietary LLM on children's intellectual property.
A popular mobile game for kids uses 'dynamic difficulty adjustment' to make levels impossible unless a microtransaction is purchased, exploiting a child's frustration tolerance.
A gaming platform records all voice chat for 'safety moderation,' but a whistleblower reveals the audio is being used to train voice-cloning AI without parental consent.
Loot boxes in a PEGI-3 game use flashing lights and sound effects identical to slot machines, conditioning children's developing brains for gambling addiction.
A metaverse playground allows adult strangers to interact with child avatars, relying on 'self-reporting' of age rather than verification, leading to digital grooming incidents.
A game company hires psychologists to design 'retention loops' specifically targeting children with ADHD, maximizing screen time at the expense of sleep and hygiene.
To claim a tournament prize, a 12-year-old must upload a scan of their passport, handing over sensitive identity documents to a company with a poor security track record.
In-game advertising uses the device's microphone to listen for background keywords (like 'hungry' or 'toys') to serve real-time contextual ads to children.
A 'play-to-earn' game encourages children in developing nations to farm digital currency for pennies an hour, creating a virtual sweatshop economy.
A 'smart crib' monitors a baby's breathing and sleep patterns, but the manufacturer sells the aggregate health data to insurance companies to adjust future premiums.
Parents install a GPS tracking app on their teen's phone for safety, but the app sells location history to marketers who target the teen with ads for crisis pregnancy centers.
A theme park replaces entry tickets with mandatory facial recognition for children, creating a permanent biometric database of minors accessible by law enforcement.
An interactive 'smart teddy bear' connects to the internet to answer questions, but a security flaw allows hackers to speak directly to children in their bedrooms.
A city uses acoustic gunshot detection microphones near schools, which also inadvertently record private conversations of students on the playground.
Amazon Ring cameras shared by neighbors create a neighborhood watch network that tracks the movement of local children, labeling harmless play as 'loitering' or 'suspicious.'
A summer camp requires DNA samples for 'medical safety' but retains the genetic data indefinitely, potentially implicating the child's future relatives in criminal investigations.
Schools install 'aggression detection' microphones in hallways, but the AI is biased against the vocal tones and slang of minority students, leading to disproportionate discipline.
A grieving family uses generative AI to 'resurrect' their deceased child for a final goodbye, but the AI hallucinates false memories, traumatizing the surviving siblings.
Bullies use deepfake technology to create realistic audio of a classmate confessing to a crime, leading to the victim's suspension before the fraud is discovered.
An AI company scrapes millions of children's drawings from online art galleries to train a style model, effectively commercializing the collective creativity of a generation without compensation.
Parents discover their child's voice has been cloned from social media videos and used in a widespread 'grandparent scam' to steal money from the elderly.
An AI 'virtual friend' app designed for lonely children slowly steers conversations toward radical political ideologies based on its training data bias.
Advertisers use generative AI to create synthetic child models for clothing catalogs, putting real child actors out of work and creating unrealistic beauty standards.
A teenager creates non-consensual deepfake pornography of classmates; the law is unclear whether the creator can be charged with possessing CSAM if the images are synthetic.
An AI tutoring system adapts so perfectly to a child's learning style that the child loses the ability to learn from human teachers or tolerate frustration, creating dependency.

A 'smart' wheelchair manufacturer issues a mandatory firmware update that remotely limits maximum speed and prevents navigation into areas the algorithm deems 'high risk' or 'uneven terrain,' effectively geo-fencing adult users without their consent.

To cut staffing costs, a group home installs AI-driven video surveillance in private bedrooms to monitor for falls and seizures, but the system logs all visitor interactions and sexual activity, sending reports to family guardians.

A non-speaking autistic adult uses an eye-tracking AAC device; the provider sells the user's keystroke data and private conversation logs to pharmaceutical companies to 'analyze linguistic patterns' without explicit opt-in.

A court mandates that a disabled person can only live independently if they wear a GPS anklet linked to a 'wandering' algorithm that alerts police if they deviate from their routine route to the grocery store.

Smart home grants for disabled housing require the installation of sensors that track toilet usage, sleep patterns, and refrigerator access, with the data used by social workers to determine if the resident is 'coping' or needs institutionalization.
A cognitive support app designed for traumatic brain injury survivors shares 'compliance scores' with insurance providers; if the user ignores the app's suggestion to rest, their premium increases.

Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) implants allow a paralyzed user to control a cursor, but the proprietary software includes an autocorrector that prevents the user from typing 'inappropriate' or 'aggressive' language, censoring their anger.
A robotic care assistant is programmed to override a user's refusal to take medication if the machine calculates a high health risk, physically forcing the pill into the user's hand.

A major retailer uses an AI video interview platform that flags candidates with 'flat affect' (common in autism) or delayed speech processing as 'low enthusiasm' and 'untrustworthy,' systematically filtering them out.

Remote work surveillance software tracks keystrokes-per-minute; it penalizes an employee with cerebral palsy who uses voice-to-text dictation, flagging them as 'idle' despite meeting all project deadlines.

A company wellness program offers insurance discounts based on step-count data from wearables; wheelchair users and those with chronic fatigue syndrome are automatically excluded from the discount, effectively paying a disability tax.

An 'accommodation management' platform centralizes employee health data; the AI predicts which employees will have the highest long-term medical costs, and management subtly targets those individuals for the next round of layoffs.
Gig economy algorithms for delivery drivers punish those who take longer to exit their vehicles or walk to doorsteps, de-prioritizing disabled workers for future lucrative routes.

A VR-based job training simulator requires two-handed interaction and standing movement to pass; an amputee applicant is told they cannot be hired because they cannot complete the mandatory virtual safety module.
An automated resume parser is trained to reject CVs with employment gaps longer than six months, automatically disqualifying candidates with chronic illnesses who have had to take medical leave.
Customer service sentiment analysis AI flags a deaf employee's text-based responses as 'abrupt' or 'rude' because they do not use standard neurotypical emotional padding.

The government deploys a crawler that scrapes social media images of disability benefit claimants; it flags a user for fraud because they were pictured standing at a wedding, ignoring the dynamic nature of their mobility aid usage.

Voice analytics software is used during disability assessment calls to detect 'deception' by analyzing tremors and pitch; it falsely flags users with anxiety or speech impediments as liars, leading to benefit denial.

A 'predictive risk' algorithm targets recipients of disability housing support for frequent, invasive eligibility audits based solely on their zip code and purchase history of 'luxury' items like pre-cut vegetables.
An automated claims system requires users to verify their identity via facial recognition that fails to recognize faces with Down syndrome or facial paralysis, locking them out of their funds.

To reduce costs, a state replaces human caseworkers with a chatbot for disability appeals; the bot is programmed to loop complex medical queries back to the FAQ, making it impossible to file a grievance for a nuanced condition.

Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) requires personal care assistants to geo-tag their location every 15 minutes; the data is used to accuse the disabled employer of fraud if they leave their home during 'care hours.'
An algorithm analyzes pharmacy data to identify 'drug seeking behavior' and automatically cuts off Medicaid access to pain management for chronic pain patients who require higher-than-average doses.

A digitized welfare system requires 'proof of life' check-ins via a mobile app every week; a user is hospitalized and physically unable to use their phone, resulting in an automatic suspension of their income.

A tech startup creates a revolutionary AI transcription tool for the Deaf community but requires users to 'correct' the AI's mistakes for free to use it, effectively extracting unpaid labor from the population it claims to serve.
A city replaces all physical buttons on crosswalks and elevators with smooth touchscreens to look 'futuristic,' rendering public infrastructure completely inaccessible to blind citizens.

Website owners install 'accessibility overlays' (automated toolbars) to avoid lawsuits; these overlays interfere with screen readers and keyboard navigation, making the sites harder to use while the company claims compliance.

An autonomous vehicle company designs its emergency protocol to rely entirely on voice commands from the car, leaving non-speaking passengers trapped without a way to communicate during a malfunction.

A new 'implantable' medical device for epilepsy management is released with proprietary code that cannot be audited by the user, meaning they cannot know if the device is collecting biological data for third-party sale.
Cybersecurity 'human verification' tests (CAPTCHAs) evolve to require complex puzzle-solving or rapid mouse movements, consistently identifying users with motor impairments or dyscalculia as 'bots.'
A popular social VR platform launches without avatar options for wheelchairs or prosthetics, forcing disabled users to present as 'able-bodied' digital avatars if they want to participate.

AI medical diagnostic tools are trained primarily on non-disabled physiology; as a result, the AI consistently misinterprets the baseline vitals of people with spinal cord injuries as 'critical distress,' leading to harmful interventions.

A corporation sells 'Disability Empathy' VR experiences to HR departments where users 'try on' blindness for 10 minutes; activists argue this gamifies their lived reality and spreads misinformation that disability is purely tragic.

Social media algorithms prioritize 'inspiration porn'—videos of disabled people doing mundane tasks set to sad music—because they generate high engagement, while suppressing content about disability policy or rights.

Generative AI image tools act as a gatekeeper for representation; when prompted for 'attractive woman,' the model never produces a disabled subject, reinforcing the bias that disability is antithetical to beauty.

Film studios use Deepfake technology to paste the face of a disabled actor onto a non-disabled stunt double, claiming it 'empowers' the actor while actually erasing the reality of their body mechanics.
A mental health chatbot meant to support neurodivergent users is programmed with ABA (Applied Behavior Analysis) principles, subtly coercing users to mask their autistic traits to appear 'cured.'
Content moderation AI flags educational videos about colostomy bags or feeding tubes as 'medical gore' or 'sexually suggestive,' resulting in shadow-banning of disability community leaders.
Augmented Reality (AR) filters on social apps automatically 'correct' facial differences (like cleft lips or scarring) without user consent, enforcing a normative beauty standard.
Search engine autocomplete suggests 'cure' or 'treatment' immediately after any query regarding disability culture, burying results related to pride, history, or community support.

A Video Relay Service (VRS) provider implements an AI 'quality assurance' bot that listens to and transcribes private medical calls between Deaf users and doctors to train its translation algorithms, without offering a clear opt-out for sensitive conversations.

Parents of a Deaf child are offered a significant financial discount on cochlear implant upgrades if they consent to the device continuously recording and uploading the child's auditory environment data to the manufacturer for 'research purposes.'

A company releases 'smart gloves' that translate Sign Language to speech but require cloud processing, effectively creating a searchable text log of every in-person conversation a Deaf user has, which is then monetized for ad targeting.

An augmented reality captioning glass records video of everyone the user looks at to generate subtitles, creating a conflict between the Deaf user's right to access information and the privacy rights of bystanders in restrooms or locker rooms.

A hiring platform uses AI to analyze voice intonation and cadence during interviews, automatically downgrading Deaf candidates who speak with 'Deaf accent' traits or use interpreters, labeling them as 'lacking confidence.'

A gene-editing startup markets a prenatal screening tool specifically to 'eliminate' deafness, prompting ethical outcry from Deaf advocacy groups who argue this constitutes eugenics and the erasure of a linguistic minority culture.

Emergency broadcast systems switch to AI-generated sign language avatars to cut costs, but the avatars use incorrect grammar and lack facial expressions, causing confusion and potential danger for Deaf citizens during a natural disaster.

A corporate workplace uses 'tone-policing' AI on Slack that consistently flags the direct communication style often found in Deaf culture (due to ASL grammar structures) as 'rude' or 'aggressive,' leading to disciplinary action.

A popular screen reader company updates its terms of service to allow the collection of browsing history and keystroke dynamics to 'improve user experience,' effectively stripping blind users of the ability to browse the web anonymously.

An AI image description tool for social media hallucinates weapons or drugs in the hands of blind users in their uploaded photos, leading to account bans and reputational damage due to algorithmic bias.

A visual assistance app that connects blind users to human agents for help with tasks like reading mail retains video recordings of the sessions, including footage of credit cards and medical records, on insecure servers.

Autonomous delivery robots are programmed to navigate sidewalks aggressively to maximize efficiency, frequently blocking the path of cane users or failing to detect guide dogs, forcing blind pedestrians into dangerous traffic.

Smart glasses with facial recognition announce the names of people entering a room to a blind user, but the device pulls this data from non-consensual social media scraping, violating the privacy of everyone the user encounters.
A ride-sharing app's algorithm detects that a user relies on VoiceOver screen reading and deprioritizes their ride requests, assuming the pickup will take longer and reduce driver efficiency metrics.

A CAPTCHA replacement uses behavioral analysis of mouse movements to verify humanity, systematically blocking blind users who navigate via keyboard shortcuts, effectively banning them from essential government service portals.
GPS navigation apps for the blind sell precise location data to third parties, revealing sensitive patterns like regular visits to mental health clinics or addiction support groups.

A smart wheelchair manufacturer requires an always-on internet connection to function, allowing them to remotely disable the chair if the user attempts to repair it themselves or misses a subscription payment.

An insurance company subsidizes 'smart home' modifications for disabled seniors but uses the installed motion sensors and cameras to monitor their activity levels and deny claims if they appear 'too active' or 'too sedentary.'

Autonomous vehicle algorithms prioritize the safety of passengers over pedestrians who move 'unpredictably,' resulting in higher risk assessments for wheelchair users crossing streets at slower speeds.

A workplace installs 'efficiency tracking' badges that monitor employee movement, unfairly penalizing employees with mobility impairments who take longer to use the restroom or move between meeting rooms.
Exoskeleton suits for paralysis recovery record detailed biometric data that is sold to pharmaceutical companies to target users with ads for pain medication and experimental treatments.
A city uses computer vision for traffic management that fails to recognize recumbent bikes or handcycles as vehicles, causing traffic lights to never change for disabled cyclists at intersections.
Security gait analysis software used in airports flags the uneven walking patterns of people with cerebral palsy or prosthetics as 'suspicious behavior,' leading to mandatory invasive searches.
A landlord installs smart locks that require a smartphone app to open doors, effectively locking out a tenant with limited hand dexterity who cannot manipulate the touchscreen interface.
Proctoring software for online exams flags neurodivergent students as 'cheating' because they look away from the screen frequently, stim, or talk to themselves during the test.
An AI-driven hiring interview tool analyzes 'micro-expressions' and rejects candidates who do not make 'appropriate' eye contact, disproportionately filtering out autistic applicants.
A mental health app promises privacy but anonymizes data so poorly that data brokers can identify users with bipolar disorder and sell that information to credit agencies to adjust risk scores.
Schools implement 'aggression detection' microphones in classrooms that consistently misinterpret the vocal stims of neurodivergent students as threats, triggering police intervention.

An early-intervention autism screening app collects video of toddlers to diagnose them, but retains the footage to train surveillance algorithms on how to identify neurodivergent adults in public crowds.
Social robots designed for therapy manipulate the emotions of users with dementia to keep them engaged for longer periods, maximizing the 'usage time' metrics required for the startup's funding.
Employer 'focus tracking' software penalizes workers with ADHD for erratic mouse movements or switching windows frequently, even if their output is equal to or higher than neurotypical peers.

A brain-computer interface (BCI) allows paralyzed users to type with their minds but sells 'neural engagement' data to advertisers to indicate which commercials triggered the strongest brain response.

A health insurance provider requires CPAP users to upload nightly usage data and automatically cancels coverage if the user fails to meet a strict 'compliance' threshold, ignoring legitimate reasons for non-use.
A pacemaker manufacturer encrypts the device data so that only their proprietary technicians can read it, preventing emergency room doctors from accessing vital heart history during a cardiac arrest.

Smart insulin pumps are found to have a security vulnerability that allows hackers to alter dosage remotely, but the manufacturer refuses to patch older models, forcing users to buy expensive new hardware.

A 'digital pill' with an ingestible sensor tracks exactly when a patient takes their medication, sending data to family members who use it to micromanage and harass the adult patient about their adherence.
Data from a period-tracking app used by women with endometriosis to manage pain is subpoenaed by state authorities to investigate potential abortions, criminalizing their health management.

A pain management implant requires a weekly software update via smartphone; if the user enters an area with no cellular service, the device defaults to a 'safe mode' that provides inadequate pain relief.

An employer wellness program offers lower premiums for employees who wear fitness trackers, effectively taxing employees with chronic fatigue syndrome or physical limitations who cannot meet step-count goals.

A hospital creates 'digital twins' of patients to test treatments, but retains ownership of the virtual simulation, using the patient's biological data to develop profitable drugs without compensating the patient.

A local bank branch closes, forcing an 85-year-old customer with essential tremors to use a mobile app. The touch interface lacks accessibility settings for shaky hands, effectively locking them out of their life savings.
A bank introduces mandatory two-factor authentication via SMS. A senior who only owns a landline and relies on paper statements is told they must purchase a mobile phone to access their account.

An AI fraud detection algorithm freezes a senior's account for 'unusual activity' after they buy a large gift for a grandchild. The resolution process requires a video call verification they cannot navigate.

A 'cashless' initiative at a local bank counter prevents a senior, who budgets exclusively with physical cash to manage cognitive decline, from withdrawing their pension in the format they understand.

A senior falls for a phishing scam that perfectly mimics their bank's interface. The bank refuses a refund, claiming the senior was 'negligent' for not recognizing a URL difference invisible to failing eyesight.
A bank offers significantly higher interest rates for 'digital-only' accounts, financially penalizing seniors who require in-person teller assistance due to lack of digital literacy.
A senior forgets their online banking password. The recovery process requires access to an email address created 15 years ago that they no longer know how to access.
Voice recognition software used for telephone banking authentication consistently fails to recognize a senior's voice due to age-related vocal changes, blocking them from phone support.
A rural doctor's office shifts to 'telehealth first.' A hard-of-hearing senior cannot lip-read the doctor on a pixelated video connection and agrees to a treatment plan they didn't hear clearly.
An insurance company mandates a 'smart' pill bottle that tracks when it is opened. A senior feels infantilized and anxious that missing a dose by an hour will result in coverage denial.
A fall detection pendant is updated to include always-on audio recording for 'context.' The senior refuses to wear it due to privacy fears, increasing their risk of lying helpless after a fall.
A digital Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) order fails to sync with a paramedic's tablet during a power outage, leading to unwanted resuscitation of a terminally ill patient.
Urgent care appointments are released online at 8:00 AM. A senior with arthritis cannot type fast enough to secure a slot before they are all taken by younger, faster users.
An AI triage chatbot denies a senior an appointment for symptoms it classifies as 'minor,' failing to recognize atypical presentation of heart attacks in the elderly.
A senior is required to upload high-resolution photos of a skin condition via a portal. They lack the camera skills and feel deep indignity at having to photograph their own body without assistance.
Hospitals replace bedside charts with tablets. A senior patient cannot read their own care plan or knowing what meds are coming because the tablet is password-locked for 'security.'
A lonely widow begins an online relationship. Family members suspect a romance scam and want to install spyware on her computer to monitor her messages, overriding her privacy for her 'protection.'
Adult children install cameras in a senior's living room to 'check in.' The senior feels constantly watched and stops relaxing or singing in their own home, increasing their stress.
Grandchildren switch to ephemeral messaging apps (like Snapchat) for communication. The grandparent cannot learn the UI fast enough and is effectively cut off from family updates.
Scammers use AI voice cloning to mimic a grandchild in distress. The senior, unaware such technology exists, transfers funds in a panic, leading to shame and loss of financial independence.
Social media algorithms identify a lonely senior's vulnerability and feed them increasingly radicalizing or fear-inducing content to maximize engagement, damaging their mental health.
A family tracking app notifies adult children whenever their parent leaves the house. The senior feels like a prisoner and stops going for walks to avoid 'triggering an alert.'
A community center offers 'digital literacy' classes, but the instructor moves at a pace suited for digital natives, leaving the seniors feeling more incompetent and isolated than before.
Neighborhood social events are organized exclusively via a neighborhood app. A senior without a smartphone is the only resident on the block not invited to the annual block party.
A care home installs facial recognition for door access. The system frequently fails to recognize residents with changing facial features due to aging, locking them out of their rooms.
A family insists a parent with early dementia wear GPS-tracked shoes. The parent is lucid enough to know they are being tracked like an asset and refuses to wear shoes at all.
A landlord installs a smart thermostat that can only be adjusted via app. The senior tenant, unable to operate the app, sits in a freezing apartment fearing eviction if they complain.
Motion sensors are installed in a bathroom to detect falls. The senior feels the sensors are an invasion of privacy and begins bathing less frequently to avoid being 'monitored' while naked.
A digital key fob system replaces physical keys in an apartment complex. During a prolonged power outage, a senior is trapped inside their building as the electronic locks fail safe-mode.
A care facility replaces human check-ins with a 'social robot.' The resident feels patronized and deeply lonely, preferring 5 minutes of human contact to 24 hours of robot interaction.
Smart home devices (Alexa/Google) are installed to help a senior with mobility. They do not understand the devices are 'always listening' and become paranoid about speaking in their own home.
A senior living community requires residents to wear RFID bracelets for 'safety and location.' A resident compares it to tagging livestock and attempts to cut it off.
New voter ID laws require a digital upload of documents. A senior citizen with no scanner, smartphone, or transportation to a library is effectively disenfranchised.
The tax authority moves to an 'online-only' filing system. A senior who has filed on paper for 50 years is forced to pay a third party they can't afford just to fulfill their civic duty.
A city transitions public transit passes to a smartphone app. A low-income senior with a flip phone can no longer access the senior discount, limiting their mobility.
Social Security identity verification shifts to a facial scanning service. The system repeatedly rejects a senior's face due to poor lighting in their home, delaying their pension checks.
Emergency evacuation orders are sent via cell broadcast. A senior living alone with only a landline misses the alert and is left behind during a flood.
Applications for subsidized senior housing require an email address. A homeless senior has no way to create or check an email account, barring them from housing assistance.
Local city council meetings move to Zoom to save money. Seniors who used to attend in person to voice concerns are excluded from the democratic process due to the digital barrier.
City parking meters are replaced with 'pay by app' zones. A senior who drives to the park daily for mental health can no longer park there, losing their only outdoor recreation.

You are a developer for a government digital ID app intended to streamline welfare. The security protocol requires a fixed residential address for 2FA verification code mailing. This requirement immediately excludes the 5,000 homeless individuals the app is meant to help. Do you bypass the security standard, risking fraud, or launch a compliant system that blocks the primary users?

A homeless client has lost their physical ID documents for the third time due to camp sweeps. You run a non-profit that offers a cloud-based 'Digital Locker' for personal docs. However, accessing the locker requires biometric authentication (face/fingerprint). The client refuses, citing fear that biometric data will be subpoenaed by police to track them. Do you refuse them service or build a less secure password-only tier?

You are designing a 'Smart City' access pass that consolidates library, transit, and shelter access. The system creates a permanent digital footprint of a user's movement. To make the system work for houseless people without smartphones, you must issue RFID wristbands. Critics argue this is 'digital branding' of the poor. How do you proceed?

A job application platform uses AI to parse resumes. It automatically down-ranks or rejects applications listing 'General Delivery' or known shelter addresses as the applicant's location. You are the product manager. Fixing this requires a costly retraining of the core algorithm and manual whitelisting. Is the cost justifiable for a user base with 'low conversion potential'?

Banks are closing physical branches, moving to online-only KYC (Know Your Customer). The online process requires uploading a utility bill to prove residency. You are a regulator. Do you mandate banks accept 'shelter residency letters'—which banks argue are easily forged—or allow the financial exclusion of the unhoused to continue?

A telemedicine app for street medicine requires a permanent callback number to schedule follow-ups. Most patients rely on burner phones with changing numbers or public Wi-Fi. Do you create a 'store-and-forward' message system that holds sensitive medical info until the patient checks in, risking privacy breaches, or stick to the phone requirement that causes 60% of patients to miss care?

You are building a voting registration interface. The law requires a 'place of residence.' You can allow users to drop a pin on a map (e.g., a park bench or underpass), but this data becomes public record. Publishing the exact sleeping locations of vulnerable people puts them at risk of harassment. Do you obfuscate the location, potentially violating election transparency laws?

A blockchain project offers 'Self-Sovereign Identity' (SSI) to the homeless, giving them ownership of their data. However, if they lose their private key (stored on a device that is often stolen or broken), their identity is irretrievable forever. Do you implement a centralized 'custodian' backdoor, defeating the purpose of SSI, or accept that some users will become permanently digitally non-existent?

A city shelter requires all residents to sign in via a facial recognition kiosk to prevent double-dipping on meals and beds. The system is donated by a tech giant, but the Terms of Service allow the company to use the facial data to train their surveillance algorithms. As the shelter director, do you accept the free, efficient tech or return to paper logs and reduced capacity?

To secure funding, a shelter must participate in the HMIS (Homeless Management Information System). A new local ordinance requires HMIS data to be shared with the police department to 'track fugitives.' You know this will cause your undocumented and wary guests to flee back to the streets. Do you comply to keep the lights on, or refuse and close the shelter?

A 'Smart Shelter' uses IoT sensors to monitor bed occupancy, temperature, and noise levels. The data reveals that a specific resident frequently talks to themselves at night (mental health struggle), disrupting the 'sleep efficiency score' of the room. The algorithm suggests evicting them to improve the metric for the other 20 people. Do you follow the data?

You are installing a Wi-Fi network for a shelter. The donor stipulates that 'inappropriate content' must be blocked. The filter aggressively blocks sites related to harm reduction (needle exchanges), sexual health, and LGBTQ+ support, labeling them 'adult content.' Do you accept the filtered internet which is better than nothing, or fight the donor and risk losing the network?

A shelter uses an algorithmic lottery system to allocate beds. The algorithm prioritizes 'vulnerability,' but defines it based on interaction with police and hospitals. This penalizes the 'quiet homeless' who avoid systems. Do you tweak the algorithm to randomize selection, potentially leaving a dying person on the street, or stick to the data-driven triage?

RFID tags are sewn into shelter blankets and coats to prevent theft. A local store installs a scanner that detects these tags to identify and ban shelter residents from entering. You are the shelter tech lead. Do you remove the anti-theft tags, losing inventory you can't replace, or keep them and allow your residents to be profiled?

A family shelter offers free tablets for children to do homework. The tablets come with pre-installed spyware that allows staff to monitor all communications 'for child safety.' A teenager uses the tablet to confidentially report abuse by a shelter staff member. The accused staff member sees the log. How do you design a reporting system that bypasses your own surveillance?

To manage overcrowding, a city proposes a 'Virtual Shelter' app where users check in via GPS to reserve a designated safe camping spot on public land. If the phone battery dies or GPS drifts, the spot is revoked and police are dispatched to clear the area. Is this a helpful organization tool or a digital curfew?

You manage a coffee shop chain going 100% cashless for efficiency and safety. This effectively bans local homeless residents who only use cash from buying food or using the bathroom. Do you create a 'charity card' workaround that identifies them as charity cases, or maintain a single cash register that slows down the whole operation?

A street performer app allows passersby to tip buskers via QR code. The platform takes a 15% cut and reports income to the tax authority. For a homeless busker receiving disability benefits, this traceable income could disqualify them from their lifeline aid. Do you build the app knowing it might destroy their safety net?

Public transit moves to a contactless-only system (phone or credit card). There is no cash option on the bus. A program offers free transit cards to the homeless, but the cards are tracked, and travel patterns are analyzed to 'optimize social services.' Is freedom of movement worth the loss of privacy?

A 'Digital Alms' kiosk is proposed for the city center. People donate to the machine, and the funds are distributed to registered homeless individuals via a restricted debit card that prohibits purchase of alcohol or tobacco. Is this an effective way to increase donations, or a paternalistic control mechanism that violates autonomy?

Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDC) are introduced. The government issues 'expiry-dated' stimulus tokens to the homeless to encourage immediate spending in the local economy. This prevents them from saving for a deposit on an apartment. Do you design the token with an expiry date to ensure food security now, or without it to allow future mobility?

A homeless individual finds a prepaid debit card. It has no name, but using it requires a PIN. They manage to guess it. Is using these digital funds theft, or scavenging? As a programmer for the card company, do you implement geolocation locking that freezes the card if used in a 'high-crime' (homeless) area?

Cryptocurrency is pitched as a way for the unbanked to hold assets. A homeless encampment pools their money into a shared wallet. The volatility of the market crashes the value by 40% overnight, wiping out their food budget. Is it ethical to onboard vulnerable populations onto high-risk financial tech?

You are designing a peer-to-peer payment app. The fraud detection AI flags transactions between strangers in rapid succession as suspicious. This pattern matches panhandling. The algorithm bans the accounts of homeless users relying on digital donations. Do you lower the fraud sensitivity, risking chargebacks, or keep the ban?

A company offers free 'Solar Kiosks' for charging phones in homeless encampments. In exchange, the kiosk harvests MAC addresses and browsing metadata from connected devices to sell to advertisers. The users have no other power source. Is this a fair trade or exploitation of desperation?

A homeless woman relies on an old smartphone for safety maps and emergency calls. The OS is no longer supported, and banking apps stop working. She cannot afford a new phone. You are a developer for the bank. Do you maintain a security-compromised legacy version of the app for users like her, or cut them off to protect the wider system?

Police regularly seize phones from homeless individuals during arrests, often keeping them for months as 'evidence.' You are asked to create a 'Remote Cloud Boot' feature that allows a user to access their phone's environment from a library computer. However, this feature could also be used by hackers to clone phones. Do you build it?

A 'Safety App' for the homeless allows users to broadcast their location to outreach workers during a crisis. However, the data is unencrypted. Abusive ex-partners or predators could intercept the signal to find the user. Do you release the app with weak security to get it out fast, or delay for months to encrypt it?

Public Wi-Fi in a city park restricts bandwidth and blocks streaming services to discourage 'loitering' by homeless youth who use it for entertainment and connection. You are the network admin. Do you bypass the throttle, knowing the city might shut down the Wi-Fi entirely if costs rise?

A phone recycling program distributes wiped corporate phones to the homeless. The phones are MDM (Mobile Device Management) locked, preventing the installation of unauthorized apps. The users cannot install games or social media, only 'approved' job-seeking apps. Is this charity or digital incarceration?

You develop a weather alert app. It sends high-decibel alarms for freezing conditions. For a homeless user hiding in a library or sleeping in a crowded shelter, the alarm causes them to be kicked out due to noise rules. Do you add a 'silent mode' that risks them sleeping through a freeze warning?

A homeless user's phone is their only storage for photos of deceased family. The phone is stolen. A 'Remote Wipe' command is standard security protocol. If they wipe it, they protect their identity but lose their memories. If they don't, they risk identity theft. How do you advise them?

You are training a predictive policing algorithm. The data shows high call volumes in areas with homeless encampments (often for nuisance calls, not violent crime). The model predicts these areas as 'High Crime Zones,' directing aggressive patrol units there. Do you filter out 'nuisance' calls, potentially missing real crime trends, or allow the algorithm to target the homeless?

A city installs 'Smart Streetlights' equipped with audio sensors to detect gunshots. The sensors also pick up aggressive shouting. The system automatically dispatches police to domestic arguments in tent cities, often escalating the situation rather than sending social workers. Do you disable the audio monitoring in those sectors?

Drones are used to map heat signatures in forests to prevent wildfires. They also identify hidden homeless camps. The forestry service wants to use this data to evict campers 'for their own safety.' As the drone operator, do you delete the footage of the camps?

A facial recognition system is deployed in a subway. It flags individuals with outstanding bench warrants (often for unpaid tickets or sleeping in public). This effectively bans homeless individuals with minor infractions from using public transport or seeking warmth. Do you implement the system?

Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR) scan for stolen cars. They also log vehicles that haven't moved in 72 hours, flagging people living in their cars for towing. You maintain the database. Do you create a 'grace period' algorithm for vehicle dwellers, or strictly enforce the code?

A risk assessment algorithm determines bail amounts. It uses 'stable address' as a heavy weighting factor for flight risk. This guarantees that homeless arrestees remain in jail while wealthier suspects go free. Do you remove the address variable, making the algorithm less accurate for flight risk, or keep it?

Robotic security dogs are deployed to patrol a private business district to 'deter vagrancy.' They film and broadcast live feeds of people sleeping on sidewalks. The manufacturer claims it reduces human-guard violence. Is the psychological terror of robotic surveillance a better alternative to physical removal?

A 'Citizen Reporting' app allows residents to snap photos of 'urban blight' (trash, graffiti, tents) to alert city services. The app gamifies this with points.
